summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a man with secondary progressive multiple sclerosis, neurogenic bladder with chronic Foley catheter, and a history of recurrent UTIs, was admitted for worsening leg weakness and found to have a urinary tract infection due to E. coli. He was treated with IV ampicillin-sulbactam after culture confirmed sensitivity, having initially been on cefepime. His weakness, attributed to a recrudescence of myelopathy triggered by infection, improved with treatment. A bladder stone found at the catheter tip was sent for pathology, and urology recommended outpatient cystolitholapaxy to prevent future infections. Pressure ulcers on the left hip and right buttock were managed with bedside debridement and ongoing wound care. His fluoxetine was increased for depression, and he was discharged to extended care with a seven-day course of IV antibiotics, pending follow-up for stone results, urology, neurology, and wound management.
